title: Provable Adaptivity of Adam under Non-uniform Smoothness

problem.claim: Theoretical analysis of Adam remains unsatisfactory, particularly because existing convergence analyses rely on globally bounded smoothness.

gap.claim: The bounded smoothness assumption does not hold for many deep learning tasks and obscures Adam's adaptation to local smoothness.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes the convergence of randomly reshuffled Adam with diminishing learning rate under the (L0, L1)-smooth condition, where smoothness is linearly bounded by the gradient norm.
The paper refines an existing lower bound for SGD and shows that SGD can be slower than Adam when both use diminishing learning rates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that randomly reshuffled Adam maintains convergence properties when smoothness is linearly bounded by the gradient norm.
The authors report that SGD can be slower than Adam under diminishing learning rates.
The authors report that the comparison reveals an advantage of Adam over SGD in the shared setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Adam is widely used because of fast convergence, while its theoretical analysis remains unsatisfactory.
Existing analyses rely on bounded smoothness, an assumption that may fail in deep learning and obscure Adam's local adaptation.
The paper studies randomly reshuffled Adam with diminishing learning rate.
The authors present convergence analysis without bounded smoothness and under smoothness linearly bounded by the gradient norm.
The paper compares Adam and SGD with diminishing learning rates and reports that SGD can be slower than Adam.

source_observation.claim: Adam's update magnitude can adapt according to local smoothness, while global bounded smoothness assumptions make this feature irrelevant.

interpretation.claim: Analyses that model local or gradient-dependent smoothness may better capture the mechanism attributed to adaptive optimization.

application.claim: When analyzing adaptive optimizers, consider non-uniform smoothness conditions rather than only globally bounded smoothness.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this modeling choice applies beyond randomly reshuffled Adam or the stated smoothness condition.

source_observation.claim: The authors report that SGD can be slower than Adam under diminishing learning rates in the same comparison setting.

interpretation.claim: Optimizer comparisons may reveal adaptive-method advantages when learning-rate schedules and analytical assumptions are held in a common setting.

application.claim: Compare optimization methods under matched learning-rate regimes and smoothness assumptions before attributing performance differences.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide quantitative rates, constants, or empirical conditions for the reported comparison.

unknowns: Exact convergence rates, constants, and theorem conditions are not provided.
The abstract does not specify experiments, datasets, or empirical measurements.
The relationship between randomly reshuffled Adam and other Adam variants is not detailed.
